question: Weighing MPS's cash-rich Research franchise against Stage 4 technical breakdown and newly uncovered Pass 1 risks in Education, Unbound Medicine, and Research hiring, what is our unbiased verdict across three horizons and where should marginal cash sit?

epigraph.quote: Underwriting Rule: a great business is a reason to do the work, not a reason to catch a falling knife.
epigraph.author: Research Desk house maxim

web_blocks.html: The locked decision. Pass 1's Compounder Pass is strictly provisional: strong cash conversion and 35%–39% ROCE are tempered by a 37% FY26 drop in tangible net worth (₹102.2 Cr; goodwill+intangibles 52.5% of assets), 0% dividend yield, −9.9% Q2 organic Education contraction, ₹36.3 Cr unreconciled CARO tax disputes, and the ADI BPO due-diligence disclaimer [1, 104, 107]. Our November 2026 refresh cuts new capital from wait-for-support to REJECTED (unqualified tier, zero allocation). Our Zerodha account holds 0 shares of MPSLTD (not held; zero shares to sell), so this decision covers marginal INR cash only. Two forces drive the cut. First, the chart broke cleanly into Stage 4: MPS closed at ₹2,105.60 on 23 November before dropping −2.41% to ₹2,054.80 on 25 November (1.47x 30-day volume), breaking the 200-day average (₹2,084.67) and pivot S1 (₹2,065.93) [90, 91]. Second, Pass 1's bruises (organic Education −9.9%, OpenEvidence partnering with Unbound licensor Johns Hopkins Medicine, and +20.42% ex-AJE Research pre-hiring) leave just +6.0% to +8.6% base weighted upside (+2.3% to +4.8% under Severe-Bear ₹1,336 stress) and 11.6%–11.7% M&A-adjusted IRR [99, 103, 104]. We do not catch falling Stage 4 knives.
Before locking our scenarios and action plan, we test the strongest arguments on both sides across nine pillars. Every new Pass 1 finding sits alongside MPS's confirmed cash strengths.

web_blocks.caption: Bull vs Bear: nine pillars steelmanned on both sides with our refreshed independent judgment
rows: Franchise and moat

A 56-year-old production and platform partner embedded in the world's largest scholarly publishers. Average MPS business units per star account rose from 2.5 to 5.5 over two years; ten-year operating cash flow matches net profit; ROCE remains 35% to 39% [1, 2, 18].

Lumina Datamatics completed 100% ownership of TNQTech (₹338.09 Cr FY26 turnover) and launched Editorial Central in Oct 2026; Straive signed Anthropic (3 Nov) and Microsoft Ignite (18 Nov, 700+ accelerators) AI partnerships; Springer Nature builds detection tools in-house [29, 109, 110, 111, 112].
Bull holds a narrower edge (~65%): embedded workflow relationships endure, yet rival AI platforms are catching up faster than our prior monograph assumed.
Research margins & AI hiring leverage

Q2 FY27 Research ex-AJE revenue jumped +21.71% YoY to ₹104.00 Cr at a 49.25% EBITDA margin (reported Research 48.17%), winning 42 new journals (25 more onboarding in Q3) and a 110,000+ peer-review submission mandate; EBITDA per head rose +14.6% YoY [2, 103].

Group headcount surged +11.16% YoY to 3,557 and Research ex-AJE headcount jumped +20.42% to 2,565—nearly matching revenue growth and breaking the near-flat headcount thesis. Large AI-era renewals still risk RWS-style unit-price give-back [67, 103].
Hinge claim — unproven until H2 FY27 billing: November–December mandate conversion must prove staff additions create operating leverage rather than linear labor inflation.
Education & Unbound Medicine

Reported Education revenue rose +30.03% YoY in Q2 to ₹68.68 Cr on Unbound Medicine's contribution (₹21.07 Cr Q2 / ₹41.64 Cr H1), diversifying billed clients +90% YoY to 933 and pulling top-5 share down to 46% [102, 106].

Stripping out Unbound reveals organic Education contracted −9.9% YoY in Q2 (−3.8% H1) with organic Q2 EBITDA down −23.3% [104]. Unbound's royalty-bearing third-party content model structurally caps EBITDA near ~18%, while free OpenEvidence (703,265 U.S. clinicians) just partnered with Unbound's own licensor Johns Hopkins Medicine [99, 100, 102].
Bear wins decisively until proven otherwise: Unbound's moat durability was cut from 4 to 3 in Pass 1; organic Education recovery and 90%+ institutional renewals are mandatory gates.
Corporate Learning turnaround

Clear Q2 FY27 operating inflection: revenue rose +17.01% YoY to ₹25.79 Cr (H1 +11.55% to ₹53.39 Cr) and Q2 EBITDA nearly doubled (+98.14%) to ₹6.38 Cr (24.74% margin) on 19.05% fewer staff (136 vs 168) [105].
FY26 revenue fell 16.5% after three missed recovery timelines; global peer Skillsoft is shrinking (−6% YoY); and ₹100.38 Cr of goodwill still sits on a historically volatile 12% segment [1, 48].
Bull wins the quarter, skeptic keeps the weight small: genuine margin repair earns credit, yet two quarters do not make a core compounding engine.
Customer concentration
Billed ex-B2C clients rose 90% YoY to 933; top-5 client share fell from 49% (H1 FY26) to 46% (H1 FY27); largest customer declined from 18.6% to 17.3% [1, 106].
Top 15 customers still generate 58% of consolidated revenue and three standalone accounts exceed 10% each (39.0% combined). One large re-tender can erase a year of organic growth [1].
Direction improves, level stays risky: a 15% annual probability of an adverse top-account re-pricing stays embedded in our Bear weight.
Balance sheet, cash & M&A discipline
Zero bank debt and ₹163.23 Cr cash on 30 Sep 2026 after repaying the Unbound loan in August; DSO improved sharply from 51 days (Mar 2026) to 38 days; ₹651 Cr returned over FY19–FY25 [1, 106].

Goodwill plus acquired intangibles equal 52.5% of assets; Unbound's purchase allocation remains provisional until February 2027 (88% goodwill); dividend yield is 0% while capital awaits acquisitions [1, 2].
Bull wins on liquidity, bear on acquisition overhang: debt-free cash generation protects solvency, but zero dividend means shareholders are not paid to wait through Stage 4.
Governance, talent & ADI BPO merger

Promoters hold 68.34% with zero pledges or selling; KPMG appointed internal auditors for FY27–FY29; new Company Secretary (Piyush Jain) and CRO onboarded; CRISIL ESG upgraded to 64 (Strong) [108, 114, 115].

Chief People Officer resigned in July 2026 after under four months amid 28.85% attrition; ADI BPO merger awaits final NCLT Chennai sanction; merchant banker D&A Financial Services disclaimed independent financial, legal, or tax due diligence amid pending Income Tax and GST proceedings [1, 107, 108].
Slight bear until NCLT closes cleanly: governance controls improved, yet senior HR churn and an unverified holding-company tax footnote warrant caution.
Valuation

At ₹2,054.80 (25 Nov TV) and ₹2,105.60 (23 Nov ledger), MPS trades at 18.9x–19.5x TTM P/E, 16.7x–17.1x Base FY27E EPS, 10.8x–11.1x FY27E EBITDA, and a 6.1%–6.3% FCFF yield—implying ~10% year-one FCF growth [90, 91].

Still 15%–18% above the ten-year median multiple (17.6x); peers eClerx (19.1x) and Newgen (18.5x) sit at identical Stage 4 multiples; refreshed weighted upside is only +6.0% to +8.6% (+0.5% to +3.0% strict Basis A) [91].
Fairly priced, not deeply mispriced: optical cheapness lacks the margin of safety needed to fight a Stage 4 breakdown.
Technical tape
Daily RSI (29.66) and 4H RSI (27.17) are deeply oversold after a 31% pullback from the August high, creating bounce potential [91].

Confirmed Stage 4 breakdown on 25 Nov (₹2,054.80, −2.41% on 1.47x 30D volume) below 200D SMA (₹2,085), S1 (₹2,066), 30W SMA (−10.4%), and 50D SMA (−15.4%), with 9 distribution days and −32.4% 63D RS vs Nifty [90, 91].
Bear wins outright: broken 200-day floor on expanding volume with zero 4H reversal prohibits buying until a Stage 1 base and Stage 2 reclaim occur.
web_blocks.takeaway: Business quality still passes on cash generation, debt-free liquidity, and Research margins. Yet the Bear side now governs 12-month returns across three key drivers: Stage 4 breakdown, Education and Unbound pressure, and unproven H2 Research hiring leverage.

web_blocks.html: Our refreshed 12-month scenario table maps those nine pillars into Bear (30%), Base (50%), and Bull (20%) values for November 2027. We test returns against both the 23 November NSE ledger close (₹2,105.60) and the 25 November live TradingView print (₹2,054.80).

headers: Basis B value (vs ledger / live TV)

Base

FY27 meets the ₹310 Cr floor; FY28 grows ~10.6% organically as Research stabilizes in mid-40s margins, Corporate Learning holds ~24%–25%, and Unbound remains royalty-capped near 18%; multiple settles at 10Y median.
Bull
H2 Research mandate billing proves AI leverage at 47%+ margin, US state adoptions lift organic Education back to double digits, and cash-funded M&A compounds EBITDA above ₹400 Cr.

web_blocks.takeaway: Neither session close offers enough reward for the risk. Even from the 25 November live print of ₹2,054.80, expected return is +8.6% on Basis B and +3.0% on strict Basis A. Both fall short of a 13% hurdle while Bear risk sits at −22.5%.

web_blocks.html: Splitting our call across three horizons explains why we reject new capital today without writing off MPS forever.

web_blocks.caption: Three-horizon independent investment judgment for MPS Limited (as of 23 Nov 2026 ledger / 25 Nov 2026 live TV)
rows: Short-Term Trading / Momentum (1–3 months)
AVOID / REJECTED (0% allocation)
Confirmed Stage 4 breakdown at ₹2,054.80 (25 Nov TV) below 200D SMA (₹2,085), S1 (₹2,066), 30W SMA (−10.4%), and falling 50D SMA (−15.4%) on 1.47x volume; 4H turn false; no NSE F&O chain [91].
Only a completed multi-week Stage 1 base followed by a weekly breakout above the 30-week SMA (₹2,293) on ≥ 2x volume.
Medium-Term Inflection (6–18 months)
REJECTED / MONITOR ONLY (0% allocation)

Refreshed probability-weighted return (+6.0% to +8.6% Basis B; +0.5% to +3.0% Basis A) fails our hurdle while organic Education (−9.9% Q2), Research hiring (+20.4% ex-AJE), and ADI BPO tax diligence remain unresolved [103, 104, 107].
H2 FY27 proof: EBITDA ≥ ₹156 Cr, organic Education returning to positive YoY growth, Research revenue-per-head expanding at ≥ 45% margin, and Stage 2 tape reclaim.
Long-Term Compounding (3–5 years)
CONDITIONAL WATCHLIST (Provisional compounder pass, not yet investable)

Debt-free cash (₹163.23 Cr), 1.0x ten-year CFO/PAT, and 35%–39% ROCE keep compounding alive—strictly provisional given −37% FY26 tangible net worth (₹102.2 Cr), 52.5% goodwill+intangibles/assets, 0% dividend yield, ₹36.3 Cr CARO tax disputes, and ADI BPO diligence gaps [1, 99, 106, 107].
Two consecutive years proving Research holds ≥ 42%–45% margins through AI renewals, Unbound sustains ≥ 90% renewals despite OpenEvidence, and CARO/ADI BPO tax items close cleanly.
web_blocks.takeaway: Short-term momentum is broken, and medium-term inflection is unproven. Long-term compounding faces new clinical-AI and Education tests. Across all actionable horizons, cash stays on the sidelines.

web_blocks.html: Our trigger table lists the exact tape and business proofs required to re-open MPS. It also sets the red lines that would permanently break the long-term thesis.

web_blocks.caption: Re-underwriting prerequisites and permanent thesis-break triggers
rows: Re-underwrite (Tape — mandatory)
Stage 1 base + Stage 2 reclaim
Multi-week base formation followed by a Friday weekly close above the 30-week SMA (currently ₹2,293) with 10-week EMA curling upward on ≥ 2x normal weekly volume [91, 92]
Lifts the Stage 4 rejection gate so the stock can be freshly re-underwritten; never an automatic market buy.
Re-underwrite (Business — mandatory)
H2 Research billing conversion
H2 FY27 EBITDA ≥ ₹156 Cr (securing ≥ ₹310 Cr FY27 floor) with Research margin ≥ 45% and revenue-per-employee expanding as Nov–Dec peer-review and journal mandates bill [2, 103]
Resolves the Pass 1 headcount-inflation watch item and restores confidence in AI operating leverage.
Re-underwrite (Business — mandatory)
Organic Education stabilization
Education ex-Unbound returns to ≥ 0% YoY revenue growth in H2 FY27 with segment EBITDA margin recovering above 33% [104]
Confirms Q2's −9.9% organic contraction was timing noise rather than structural US K–12/Higher-Ed erosion.
Re-underwrite (Business — watch)
Unbound clinical renewal resilience
First full annual institutional renewal cycle prints ≥ 90% retention despite OpenEvidence's Johns Hopkins alliance [99, 100]
Supports restoring Unbound's moat score and stabilizes our 17.5x–19.0x multiple band.
Re-underwrite (Corporate)
Clean NCLT sanction for ADI BPO
Final NCLT Chennai order confirms zero public dilution (1,71,05,816 shares) and zero material inherited Direct or Indirect Tax liability [97, 107]
Closes the holding-company merger governance overhang.
Permanent exit / pass
Structural margin or client failure
Research margin below 42% for two straight quarters, FY27 EBITDA cut below ₹300 Cr, largest client above 20% or top-3 loss, goodwill write-down above ₹25 Cr, or dilutive ADI BPO terms
Downgrades Pass 1 business quality to fundamental fail and keeps MPS permanently off the shortlist.
web_blocks.takeaway: Every path back into MPS requires both chart repair and business proof. A lower price alone—even inside ₹1,810 to ₹1,920—never triggers a buy order without a Stage 1 base, Stage 2 reclaim, and H2 verification.

web_blocks.html: What could prove our rejection too cautious? First, MPS could be printing a washout low just under its 200-day average. If Q3 FY27 (due February 2027) delivers surging November–December peer-review billing, 48%+ Research margins, and an Education rebound, shares could snap back to ₹2,300–₹2,450 before a textbook Stage 1 base finishes. We gladly accept missing the first 10% to 15% of a V-shaped rally. At ₹2,350, today's ₹2,275 Base value leaves no margin of safety anyway. Paying for proof beats eating a Bear drop to ₹1,593 (−22.5% to −24.4%) or Severe-Bear stress to ₹1,336 (−35.0% to −36.6%). Second, management could deploy its ₹163.23 Cr cash into a high-margin proprietary platform deal at ~2x sales, bringing our 20% Bull case (₹3,080) into view. Even then, disciplined capital waits for real integration results and a rising 30-week trend.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Rejecting a good company at the wrong moment is a win
paragraphs: Most mistakes start when an analyst falls in love with a clean ten-year cash statement and ignores a broken chart. MPS still earns 35% to 39% on capital and holds ₹163 Cr of debt-free cash. None of that vanished at ₹2,055.

Yet our job is to compound capital without eating avoidable 30% to 50% drawdowns. When the 200-day floor breaks on heavy volume in the same month organic Education drops and OpenEvidence signs Johns Hopkins, stepping aside is not fear. It is the discipline that keeps cash ready for confirmed Stage 2 leaders.

web_blocks.intro: Position sizing turns our rejected call into zero portfolio risk. MPSLTD sits in our unqualified tier with 0 bps risk budget and 0.0% weight in Zerodha (verified net worth ₹42,64,305 on 23 November 2026; ₹14,20,950 or 33.3% in cash; 0 MPSLTD shares held). The ₹1,810.00–₹1,920.00 band and ₹1,750.00 floor in the table below are passive Stage 4 monitor-only markers placed below the live ₹2,054.80 close. They reconcile TradingView's broken overhead scanner levels (₹2,275–₹2,464 / ₹2,244) and are NOT live buy orders or stops. Any future entry will be sized fresh only after Stage 1 basing, Stage 2 reclaim above ₹2,293, and H2 proof.

Even a 1% block sale (1,71,058 shares) equals ~11 days of average volume (~₹35 Cr at ₹2,055) and would pressure a thin order book.
Governance offsets

KPMG appointed internal auditors for FY27–FY29; Piyush Jain appointed Company Secretary (29 Aug 2026); Papinani Radha Rani appointed CRO (21 Jul 2026); Postal Ballot open through 11 Dec 2026 for Independent Director Divya Verma [108, 113, 114]

Board compliance strengthened, though senior HR stability remains an active watch item.
web_blocks.takeaway: Nothing in the filings proves harm to public holders. Yet the merchant-banker diligence disclaimer and pending tax cases remove any rush to own MPS before the final NCLT Chennai order lands.

web_blocks.html: How to read the alert and cash panels below. Zerodha holds 0 shares of MPSLTD, so the action is not held with 0 shares to sell. Every alert row carries 0 shares and no active buy order. Alerts track the passive ₹1,810 shelf (pivot S2), the mandatory ₹2,293 weekly Stage 2 reclaim gate (which re-opens the file), and the February 2027 Q3/Unbound checkpoint. In capital redeployment, 100% of reviewed INR cash (₹14,20,950, or 33.3% of ₹42,64,305 net worth on 23 November) stays in cash. We assign 0% to shortlist benchmark Coforge (Stage 2, held at 2.06% weight; ₹2,142.30 ledger / ₹2,060.00 TV; Base ₹2,620; snapshot zone ₹1,951.99–₹2,066.72 at 1.45:1 R:R and posture BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO, with shortlist 20D-EMA dip band ₹1,951.99–₹2,036.18 at 1.67:1 R:R and dossier action ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP). Incremental adds to held names belong to the portfolio audit, and unheld Stage 2 shortlist peer IGIL (₹431.10 ledger / ₹432.50 TV) remains on wait-for-support. We also assign 0% to outside peers. Stage 4 names eClerx (₹1,465.80 TV / ₹1,511.40 ledger) and Newgen (₹413.65 TV) fail trend rules. Firstsource (₹288.90 TV / ₹283.60 ledger) earns under half MPS's ROCE with no monograph, and Cyient (₹1,151.20 TV / ₹1,160.50 ledger) is already held at 2.50% weight on wait-for-support.

Final action rule: Hold 0 shares of MPSLTD and keep 100% of reviewed cash intact. Place zero standing limit orders in the passive ₹1,810–₹1,920 band. Re-open this file only after BOTH (a) a Stage 1 base and weekly close above the 30-week SMA (₹2,293) on ≥ 2x weekly volume, AND (b) H2 FY27 results proving ≥ ₹156 Cr H2 EBITDA, Research margin ≥ 45% with rising revenue per head, and positive organic Education growth.

book_paragraphs: Everything we learned across eight chapters now converges on a single, unambiguous decision: we downgrade MPS Limited from our prior wait-for-support stance to REJECTED for new capital, with zero allocation today. Because our Zerodha account holds zero shares of MPS, nothing needs to be sold or trimmed. Our only task is protecting ₹14.21 lakh of dry INR cash—one-third of our ₹42.64 lakh net worth—from being deployed into a falling knife.

Why reject a debt-free business that earns 35 to 39 per cent on capital, holds ₹163 crore of cash, and just printed a 48 per cent margin in its flagship Research division? Because two independent alarms went off at the same time. On the chart, MPS closed at ₹2,105.60 on our 23 November NSE ledger and then sliced straight through its 200-day moving average and monthly pivot support two sessions later, finishing 25 November at ₹2,054.80 on nearly one and a half times normal volume. It now sits more than ten per cent beneath its thirty-week average and more than fifteen per cent beneath a falling fifty-day average, with zero upward turn on the four-hour chart. That is a confirmed Stage 4 breakdown.

At the exact same moment, our Pass 1 blind-spot audit found real bruises underneath the headline Q2 beat. Once you subtract acquired Unbound Medicine—whose royalty-bearing third-party licensing model structurally caps margins near eighteen per cent—organic Education revenue actually shrank almost ten per cent in Q2 and organic Education EBITDA fell twenty-three per cent. Even more concerning, free clinical-AI leader OpenEvidence reached over 703,000 monthly active American clinicians and signed an AI medical-education alliance directly with Johns Hopkins Medicine, one of Unbound's own flagship licensors. Meanwhile Research Solutions headcount jumped over twenty per cent outside AJE to staff incoming mandates, putting the near-flat headcount AI leverage narrative on probation until second-half billing converts, and the ADI BPO promoter merger still awaits final NCLT Chennai sanction alongside a merchant-banker due-diligence disclaimer and pending tax proceedings.

When you put those freshly audited realities into a twelve-month valuation, the optical allure of an 18.9 times trailing earnings multiple fades quickly. Our refreshed Base value drops from ₹2,410 to ₹2,275 on central last-twelve-months earnings of ₹130 at a ten-year median multiple of 17.5 times. Our Bear case—now carrying a thirty per cent probability—sits at ₹1,593, while our trimmed twenty per cent Bull case reaches ₹3,080. The probability-weighted value is ₹2,231: just 6.0 per cent above the 23 November ledger close and 8.6 per cent above the 25 November live print. On stricter year-end FY27 earnings, weighted value is ₹2,117—essentially zero upside against 22 to 24 per cent Bear downside.

Across our three investment horizons, the conclusion is consistent. Over the short term of one to three months, stay completely away—Stage 4 breaks chew up dip-buyers, and MPS has no NSE options chain to define risk. Over the medium term of six to eighteen months, stay rejected and monitor only until second-half results prove organic Education stabilizes and Research hiring converts into higher billing per employee. Over the long term of three to five years, keep MPS on a conditional compounder watchlist—its cash conversion and debt-free franchise remain genuinely valuable, provided AI renewals and clinical-AI competition do not permanently erode margins.

So where does our reviewed marginal cash go instead? One hundred per cent stays in INR cash. Within the broader Indian IT and services universe, Stage 2 shortlist leaders like Coforge are already held in our portfolio and sized inside our portfolio audit, while outside publishing and KPO peers eClerx and Newgen are stuck in the same Stage 4 downturn. Cash with a clear set of re-underwriting rules is never idle money—it is disciplined capital waiting for both the business proof and a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend.

book_callouts.title: THE TWO-KEY RULE TO RE-OPEN MPSLTD
book_callouts.quote: A cheap multiple without a rising trend is a value trap; a rising trend without organic proof is a momentum trap.
book_callouts.text: Both keys must turn before MPS leaves our rejected list for fresh underwriting.
bullets: Key 1 (Tape): Multi-week Stage 1 base followed by a weekly close above the 30-week SMA (₹2,293) on ≥ 2x average volume with the 10-week EMA curling upward.
Key 2 (Business): H2 FY27 EBITDA ≥ ₹156 Cr, Research margin ≥ 45% with rising revenue per head, organic Education ex-Unbound back to positive YoY growth, and clean ADI BPO NCLT sanction.

book_subsections.title: Why passive reference levels are not standing buy orders
paragraphs: Notice how our execution table lists ₹1,810 to ₹1,920 with a ₹1,750 reference floor as strictly monitor-only markers rather than buy orders. Below today's ₹2,055 close, monthly pivot S2 sits at ₹1,811—roughly fifteen times forward earnings. Placing a blind limit bid there while the stock is falling in Stage 4 would break Stan Weinstein's cardinal rule and ignore the fundamental questions we just uncovered in Education and Unbound Medicine.

Instead, we keep our ₹14.21 lakh Zerodha cash balance intact, track the February 2027 Q3 FY27 filing and Unbound purchase-price allocation, and wait for institutional buyers to show up on the weekly chart first. If MPS proves its AI leverage and reclaims ₹2,293 on heavy volume, we will gladly re-underwrite it from a position of strength.
